Representative elements (RVE) models of F-temper alloys Now the micro-model domains (windows) near the sample surface have been prepared from the as-cast Aural-5 alloys as described in section 4.5.3.1, including 6 windows for sample 84 and 12 windows for sample 47 and can be used for micro-model calculations, where their boundaries are driven by the displacement history recorded from the macro-models. The flow property of the eutectic is taken to be L =(102.0,1703,0.5302), while that of the dendrite taken to be L =(30.0,288,0.21). 18 RVE models are Eu Al created and calculated, and the load displacement curves are plotted in Fig. 28(a). And the critical displacement values at maximum load are [5.456, 5.84, 5.264, 5.632, 5.344, 5.552, 4.96, 5.024, 5.04, 5.28, 5.104, 5.12, 5.488, 4.912, 5.136, 5.104, 5.312, 5.536] and the average values and deviation are 5.284 and 0.25, respectively. It is apparent that the average value of 5.284 is closest to the model of (1320 1905 a1.7 e0.215.47c). From the simulation results, it is possible to track crack opening size. For such purposes, an Abaqus CAE python postprocessing code is created and Fig. 29(a) shows the results of the 18 models. It can be seen the crack opening ranges of 50 to 100 microns at the end of simulation (or at the punch displacement of 8 mm. Fig. 42(b) shows the punch displacements at the crack length 10 microns (C10) for the 18 models and the average value is 5.578 also plotted as a horizontal dashed line. The results of models (0 0 a1.7 e0.215) and (1650 1905 a1.7 e0.215 .47c) of 5.584 are close to the average value. The average critical punch displacement for the crack length of [5,6,10,15,20] microns for the 18 models are calculated to be [5.181, 5.338, 5.578, 5.861, 6.087111111111112] mm, respectively and are plotted in Fig. 42(c) together with error bars.
